properties.headline: Typhoon Warning issued October 18 at 3:01PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI CONTINUES WEST, AWAY FROM GUAM WATERS...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides important information and
recommended actions for people in Guam and the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Typhoon Warning continues for Guam and Rota.

Although tropical cyclone watches or warnings are not in effect
for Tinian and Saipan, possible impacts from related hazards are
still a concern.

A Flood Watch is in effect for portions of Guam and the Northern
Marianas. Please listen closely for any Flood Warnings that might
be in effect for your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 2 PM ChST...the center of Super Typhoon Champi (29W) was
located near latitude 13.0N...longitude 142.6E. This was about
150 miles west of Guam. Storm motion was west, 260 degrees, at 12
mph. Storm intensity was 150 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Super Typhoon Champi continues to move generally westward with a
slight southward turn over the last few hours, and a slight
decrease in forward speed. The eye remains very small and compact,
appearing to fill in with cloud cover in the latest visible
satellite imagery, with a width of around 5 miles across. It looks
to be going through an eyewall replacement cycle. GLD network
data shows frequent lightning within the deep convection along the
southern eyewall, which is beginning to exit radar range. Surface
observations from Guam International Airport show strong sustained
winds of 25 to 30 mph with frequent tropical storm-force gusts up
to 60 mph. At Saipan, winds are fresh to strong with gusts to 35
mph.
properties.instruction:
Tropical Storm conditions were verified on Rota earlier this
morning, and tropical storm-force gusts look to continue over the
next few hours as Super Typhoon Champi pulls away. Remain alert
and stay inside until the all-clear is given. Listen for possible
flood warnings.

NWSheadline: TYPHOON WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 9:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continuing through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and
spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain
will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat,
Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36
hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and
lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including
Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time
frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For
context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are
not historically extreme.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 17 at 11:13PM EDT until October 18 at 2:15AM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
FFWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northern Broward County in southeastern Florida...

* Until 215 AM EDT.

* At 1113 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2.5 and 4 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 2 to 3 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 3 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Deerfield Beach, Lighthouse Point and Hillsboro Beach.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 17 at 8:54PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Sunday, but strong northeasterly winds will slow river
flow leading to a quick rise in levels. The river is forecast to
reach Moderate Flood Stage early Monday, with a steady increase
through Moderate Flood Stage forecast through the week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with
several inches of water inside homes along the river and canals.
Docks at Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely
submerged. Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with
yards completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads
flooded in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on
Juno Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 PM EDT Saturday was 2.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet Tuesday
morning. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

The next statement will be issued Sunday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 17 at 8:33PM EDT until October 20 at 5:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 2 to 4 feet of
inundation above ground level expected in low- lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 9 to 13 feet in the surf
zone. For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents,
large breaking waves, and strong longshore currents in the
surf zone.

* WHERE...Hatteras Island.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 5 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Sunday morning through
Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level is
expected in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Numerous road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible. Vulnerable portions of NC-12 may be
inundated, especially around high tide. There is a possibility
of being stranded on Hatteras Island for multiple days. This
could be life threatening if you have an emergency. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.
Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore
into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw a swimmer
or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck and back
injuries. Strong longshore currents will create dangerous
swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...This has the potential to be a long
duration event bringing more significant ocean overwash
impacts to vulnerable oceanside areas through multiple high
tide cycles into next week. Minor soundside water level rises
will also be possible.

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected. There is also a strong
north to south longshore current expected.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...From 6 AM EDT Sunday through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 17 at 6:06PM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 8
feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM CDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching
or pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles,
except those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will
be unable to be driven on the beach. This includes locations
north of Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach
erosion is expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions
and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the
best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 AM CDT SUNDAY... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 7 AM CDT SUNDAY... ...HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SUNDAY MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Tanana Flats; Eielson AFB and Salcha; Goldstream Valley and Nenana Hills; Chatanika River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area; Nenana; Northern Denali Borough; Southern Denali Borough
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 2:54PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A low in the Gulf of Alaska will will bring a front to the Alaska
Range and Central Interior Tuesday and Wednesday. There is
uncertainty with the exact strength and placement of this front
and we are currently expecting around 3 to 6 inches of snow from
the Western Alaska Range to Fairbanks. However, there is a 30%
chance for snow accumulations exceeding 6 inches in this area.
Currently, the greatest likelihood of this occurring is towards
Eielson AFB and areas east, where Winter Storm Watches are in
effect. If the front is a bit farther to the west, this chance
increases dramatically in/around Fairbanks.

There may end up being a west to east gradient where Eielson gets
6 inches or more of snow, and Fairbanks south/west only gets a
couple of inches. We will be monitoring this storm very closely
and will have more information as the details become clearer.

NWSheadline: Moderate to Heavy Snow Possible Tuesday and Wednesday

properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 17 at 5:25PM CDT until October 18 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:

caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Glacier Bay; City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 17 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
ESFAJK

A strong storm system is expected to move over the northern Alaska
Panhandle beginning Monday night and continuing through Tuesday.
Juneau and Gustavus are expected to see periods of moderate to heavy
rain for a majority of the day on Tuesday, resulting in significant
and rapid rises on small creeks and streams. Rain totals for this
event are around 2-4 inches over a 36 hour period, though expected
totals will likely change as the event moves closer. At this time,
expect to see similar impacts to the previous storm system we saw on
Friday, where Salmon River, Jordan Creek, and Montana Creek reached
either near or into minor flood stage. Additionally, ponding of water
on roads and areas of poor drainage is possible.

Stay tuned to weather.gov/juneau as we continue to assess the
situation and make updates to the forecast.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN EXPECTED ON TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Yakutat; Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan; Eastern Chichagof Island; Cape Fairweather to Lisianski Strait; City and Borough of Sitka; Admiralty Island
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 17 at 2:08PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A strong storm system is expected to move into the northern half of
the Alaska Panhandle and the northeast Gulf Coast Monday night and
continuing through Tuesday. Beginning Monday night for Yakutat and
spreading eastward into early Tuesday morning, periods of heavy rain
will begin and continue through the day on Tuesday. For Yakutat,
Sitka, Pelican, and Elfin Cove, rain totals over a period of 36
hours is around 3 to 6 inches, with higher amounts near Yakutat and
lower amounts near Sitka. For the Icy Strait corridor, including
Hoonah and northern Admiralty Island, rain totals over the same time
frame are around 2-3 inches, similar to the previous storm. For
context, these totals are uncommon for this time of year, but are
not historically extreme.

NWSheadline: HEAVY RAIN EXPEECTED ON TUESDAY

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Volusia; Coastal Indian River; Coastal St. Lucie; Coastal Martin; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands; Mainland Southern Brevard; Southern Brevard Barrier Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 17 at 9:31AM EDT until October 20 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 10
feet expected in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Monday
night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to
4 AM EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

NWSheadline: HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH LATE MONDAY NIGHT... ...HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM 11 PM THIS EVENING TO 4 AM EDT TUESDAY

currents with breaking waves of 7 to 12 ft.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast beaches.

properties.areaDesc: Icy Cape to Cape Suckling out to 15 NM
properties.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued October 13 at 3:43AM AKDT until October 20 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Southeast Alaska Coastal Waters from Dixon Entrance to
Cape Suckling out 100 NM

Wind forecasts reflect the predominant speed and direction
expected. Seas forecasts represent the average of the highest
one-third of the combined windwave and swell height.

.TODAY...E wind 25 kt. Seas 7 ft. Showers early in the morning.
Slight chance of thunderstorms.
.TONIGHT...E wind 20 kt. Seas 6 ft. Showers in the evening.
Slight chance of thunderstorms. Showers late.
.WED...E wind 15 kt increasing to 25 kt in the afternoon.
Seas 6 ft.
.WED NIGHT...E gale to 35 kt. Gusts to 50 kt. Seas 15 ft.
Rain.
.THU...E gale to 35 kt. Seas 19 ft.
.FRI...E wind 20 kt. Seas 13 ft.
.SAT...E wind 20 kt. Seas 8 ft.

NWSheadline: SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY TUESDAY

properties.description:
Offshore Waters Forecast for the US Arctic Waters

Sea forecasts represent an average of the highest one-third of
the combined wind wave and swell height. Individual waves may be
twice as high.

Moderate freezing spray.
.MON...NE winds 25 kt. Seas 9 ft. Moderate freezing spray.
.MON NIGHT...N winds 25 kt. Seas 7 ft. Moderate freezing spray.
.TUE...NE winds 20 kt. Seas 4 ft. Moderate freezing spray.
.TUE NIGHT...NE winds 15 kt. Seas 4 ft. Light freezing spray.
.WED...W winds 15 kt. Seas 3 ft.
.THU...S winds 10 kt. Seas 2 ft.
.FRI...S winds 15 kt. Seas 7 ft.
